must_fix.issue: Readers cannot tell who does the after-wedding paperwork. 'Book it for the first working days after the wedding' (Apostille section) reads to the funding parent as 'my daughter queuing at a government office on her honeymoon' (objection, medium, an accountability question), and 'Ask your Wedded Advisor to build the appointment into your plan' leaves the primary persona, the sceptic and the UHNW reader asking whether the Advisor books the Prefettura, arranges the translation and checks the comune transcription after a church wedding, or only reminds them, and whether that is included or extra. Search_visitor and the sceptic also read the line as a sales nudge inside a neutral legal section.
must_fix.fix: Make the Apostille paragraph say plainly whose step it is, from sourced facts only: the Embassy advises asking for the apostille at the Prefettura of the city where you marry and warns May to September appointments are hard to get (fact_16), so the appointment belongs in the wedding plan in the first working days after the ceremony, before anyone flies home (insider_details). Then, once in the article (the Apostille paragraph or the close, not both), say what the Wedded Advisor does using brand-facts claims only: one Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact, and confirms in writing which steps are included before you commit. That answers 'included or extra' honestly. Do NOT state that the Advisor books the Prefettura, arranges the NAATI translation, attends any office or follows up the comune transcription: none of that is in brand-facts.md. If the writer wants to say it, use [[VERIFY: does Wedded Concierge book the Prefettura apostille appointment, arrange the NAATI translation and follow up comune transcription of a church wedding?]] (logged as a human question below). Stay within 2 to 3 'Wedded Advisor' mentions in body copy, not counting the CTA anchor text and the kept compliance line.

must_fix.issue: The 'Not published:' openers read like research notes left in the copy ('reads like a note someone forgot to delete', 'Not published by whom?'). The multilingual extract paragraph confused search_visitor, who did not know what an extract was before being told no one knows if it works. The honesty itself is the sceptic's biggest trust builder and the UHNW reader's too, so the fix is phrasing only.
must_fix.fix: Rewrite both 'Not published:' lines (multilingual extract, Prefettura processing times) and the 'Not published' cell in the states table as natural sentences that keep the admission, e.g. 'No Australian agency says whether it accepts the multilingual extract on its own, so bring home the full certificate, apostilled and translated.' and 'The Prefettura does not publish processing times, so...'. For the multilingual extract, open with what it is in a few words (a short standard-form extract in several languages) before saying it does not help in Australia. Keep the meaning of every 'not published' statement; do not drop any.

must_fix.issue: The close leans on brochure and package language. 'One person from first idea to the last dance' is a turn-off for the sceptic ('brochure talk' at the point he wants facts) and generic to the primary persona ('the same end-to-end promise every planner makes'); the UHNW reader loses trust at 'what is included' (package language). The phrase is in brand-facts, but readers dislike it and the person has approved a quieter close.
must_fix.fix: Drop 'from first idea to the last dance'. Keep 'one person', 'works in your time zone', 'quotes in AUD' and 'confirms in writing' (see conflicts_resolved), and tie them to this article: the Advisor is the one contact for the route you choose and the paperwork that follows it, within brand-facts claims (see must-fix 1). Optional brand-facts addition: 'the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins'. Keep a single CTA to /wonderland-concierge with its UTM, and keep the compliance line ('Requirements change, so your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements for your dates before you book. It is not legal advice...') unchanged.

should_fix.issue: Comune, Prefettura and apostille appear together in a takeaway and through the body with no plain-English gloss. The funding parent felt she had to guess (medium) and would not want to look old-fashioned asking; search_visitor did not know what a multilingual extract was.
should_fix.fix: Gloss each term on first use, in a few words: comune (the town hall, which runs the civil register), Prefettura (the local office of Italy's Ministry of the Interior, per fact_17), apostille (a certificate that authenticates an Italian public document for use abroad, fact_17). In the takeaway a short bracket is enough, e.g. 'the comune's (town hall's) marriage certificate'. The takeaway must stay one sentence. No glossary box.

should_fix.issue: Couples who live outside Australia, or where only one partner is Australian, cannot tell whether the answer changes. The UHNW reader (Dubai) flags the domicile wording twice (medium) and asks whether a legal ceremony in Dubai or London would work; search_visitor asks the same. The SERP research shows Australians abroad and mixed-nationality couples are a real share of searchers outside Australia.
should_fix.fix: Add one or two sentences, sourced only: the Part VA test applies to any marriage valid where it took place (fact_04), and s 88D(3) applies a different age rule where neither of you is domiciled in Australia (fact_06); the Passport Office accepts a legalised, fully translated foreign certificate from Australians who live overseas, if you became a citizen before the marriage (fact_21), and Australian embassies abroad keep lists of approved translators (fact_22); for a partner who is not Australian, marriage does not give a right to live in Australia (fact_46, already in the FAQ: cross-refer, do not repeat). Do not claim a Dubai or London ceremony is or is not recognised beyond the general Part VA test. Anything else: say the Wedded Advisor confirms it for your situation, counted inside the 2 to 3 mention cap.

should_fix.issue: Four readers want to know what the change of name, apostille and NAATI translation cost and how long they take; the surname section says 'apply' and stops. Search_visitor: 'that is the very next thing I want to know'.
should_fix.fix: Within the person's standard: say once in the surname section that a fee applies and that each registry publishes its current fees and processing times on its own page, pointing to the NSW link already in the draft. No dollar figures and no timings (none are in the source pack; only the Prefettura 'hard to get May to September' warning and the 5-day church-act transmission are sourced). Printing official fees is logged as a person question, not a fix. Not must-fix per orchestrator ruling.

should_fix.issue: The divorce FAQ sits mid-FAQ on a page the funding parent will forward to family about a wedding she is paying for (lost_trust, low); the UHNW reader says it is the wrong legal question for her family (property and prenups).
should_fix.fix: Keep it (it answers a Sydney People Also Ask question, per 02-seo.json, and is sourced to fact_45) but move it to the last FAQ position, after the visa question. No property or prenup answer: nothing is sourced; see consider.

consider.issue: Queensland and the other smaller states get one hedge each; the sceptic (Brisbane) wants the form, fee, time and registry link.
consider.fix: Add the one sourced Queensland detail: if you married overseas and had already changed your name with the Registry to your partner's name, you need to change it at the Registry (fact_29). Name each registry in the table. Registry URLs are in the source pack (fact_29 to fact_33), but external links are already at the SEO limit (02-seo.json); add one only by swapping, and only if the editor agrees. No fees or timings (not sourced).

consider.issue: The two tables are hard to read on a phone: long sentences in cells, sideways scroll.
consider.fix: Cut 'Which proof suits which purpose' cells to a few words each (e.g. 'Passport, new surname | Born here: Australian name change certificate. Born overseas: legalised, translated certificate'), or turn it into short bullets. Keep both columns' facts and every fact comment.

consider.issue: 'The cost is emotional' made the sceptic expect a dollar figure.
consider.fix: Optional: 'The trade-off is emotional.' Keep the rest of the paragraph (praised by four readers).

consider.issue: Primary persona asks how close to the Italian date to hold the Australian legal ceremony.
consider.fix: Optional, one clause from fact_35: the Notice can go in up to 18 months ahead, so the legal ceremony can be set well before you fly. No claim about what most couples do.

consider.issue: Takeaway 1 repeats the intro answer; search_visitor skimmed it.
consider.fix: No change required. It is the AI-overview restatement and carries the Act name. Exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways either way.

consider.issue: The sceptic reads 'your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements' next to 'not legal advice' as a mixed message about who carries the risk.
consider.fix: No change: the compliance line is required as written. Accountability for a wrong confirmation is a deferred business answer.

consider.issue: UHNW reader asks about property and prenups under Italian law, a private civil ceremony at the venue, public notices and a non-Catholic religious ceremony.
consider.fix: Out of scope for this recognition guide and not in the source pack; venue and notices belong to the sister guide. No draft change. Candidate topics for later posts.

'As at October 2026' in the intro (sceptic, search_visitor).

s 88D and s 88G citations with the compilation number and the link to legislation.gov.au (sceptic, planner_couple).

The honesty about gaps: every 'not published' admission and the civil union gap with its [[VERIFY]] (sceptic, uhnw). Rephrase, never remove.
The trade-offs paragraph, including 'decide before you put down a venue deposit' (four readers).
The short, sourced FAQ, especially the immigration answer (search_visitor).

conflicts_resolved: 'Quotes in AUD' and 'confirms in writing what is included': uhnw (0.20) reads them as package language; planner_couple (primary, 0.40) says they answer the hidden-costs worry and funding_parent calls them what she wants to hear. Keep AUD and 'in writing'; soften 'what is included' to 'which steps are included' tied to the paperwork. The brief's reader is a 150k-budget Australian couple, not the UHNW segment.

'Not published' lines: the sceptic calls them the page's biggest trust builder, while planner_couple, funding_parent and search_visitor find the label clunky. Keep every admission and rewrite the label as a natural sentence.

Advisor mention in the Apostille section: uhnw likes that someone else carries it; the sceptic and search_visitor call it a sales nudge; the primary persona wants to know what it means. Keep one concrete, brand-facts-only line about the Advisor's role and drop the bare nudge, within the 2 to 3 mention cap.
Divorce FAQ: funding_parent and uhnw would rather not see it; SEO research shows it answers a Sydney People Also Ask question. The primary persona did not object. Keep it, move it last.

Fee figures: four readers (all but uhnw) want official fees and timings. The person's standard is 'a fee applies'. Per orchestrator, logged as a person question, not a must-fix; the writer adds no figures and no unsourced timings.

CTA tone: uhnw wants a private introduction or a direct senior line; funding_parent wants a named person and phone; planner_couple finds the CTA low-pressure and fine. Keep the single public CTA for the primary persona; named Advisor and phone line are deferred.
deferred_by_person: Wedded Concierge fee model, and whether commissions or margins are taken (sceptic). The writer may state only the brand-facts claim that the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
Deposits, deposit protection, contracts with Italian venues in English and AUD, and who is accountable if a supplier fails or a written confirmation is wrong (funding_parent, sceptic).
'From AUD' price ranges and a rough all-in cost of the paperwork (funding_parent, planner_couple, search_visitor, sceptic). Nic signs off any figure.
A named Wedded Advisor, phone line, on-the-day or after-hours contact, or private referral route (funding_parent, uhnw).
Real weddings: a couple who married legally in Australia and celebrated in Italy (planner_couple); evidence of 200 to 400 guest weddings with VIPs (uhnw).
Wedded Privileges detail (not raised; still deferred).
Whether Wedded Wonderland also organises the legal ceremony in Australia (funding_parent): not in brand-facts; human question below.
payload.gate_note: Weighted enquiry likelihood 2.20 is below 3.8 and there are 3 must-fix items, so revise (one round per G6). Not 'stop': the piece meets the brief; trust is high (weighted 4.50, primary persona 5) and every reader kept reading past the intro. Word count is already about 2,335 against the brief's 2,200 ceiling, so the writer should offset additions with trims (candidates: the consent paragraph in the s 88D section and the s 113(2) line) rather than grow the piece. Caution for the orchestrator: most of the enquiry gap comes from deferred business answers (what the Advisor does on paperwork, fee model, named Advisor, real weddings) and the decision on printing official fees; the copy fixes should lift clarity and the primary persona's confidence but are unlikely on their own to reach 3.8, so G6 should not loop on that.
